resources.string: YukariBox runs no servers of its own. You supply them: paste a share link, scan a QR code, or add a subscription URL from a provider. Everything you add stays on this device.

A group holds servers. A manual group is a list you edit yourself; a subscription is a URL that is fetched again on every update — and an update replaces that group\'s servers wholesale, keeping only your starred ones and your current choice where it still exists.

If a live session collapses and reconnecting fails, the app holds the tunnel open with nothing behind it so packets are dropped instead of leaking out unprotected. You will see "Traffic blocked" on the home screen, with a button to reconnect or to release the block deliberately.\n\nThat block lives inside YukariBox, so it goes away if Android stops the app to reclaim memory. For one that survives that, turn on Android Settings → Network → VPN → YukariBox → Always-on VPN, and "Block connections without VPN" beside it.
How do I move to a new phone?

Profile → Backup and restore writes every group to a file you choose. That file contains your server credentials in the clear unless you set a password on it, so keep it somewhere you would keep a password.
